messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - Elevated packet loss and BGP withdrawal observed to upstream ASN 64521 affecting eu-west-1 <-> us-west-2 cross-region paths. Paging: @maria (net-oncall)

maria (net-oncall): I'm on it. seeing ~40% packet loss to a handful of /24s from provider AS64521; BGP withdraws intermittently. Customers report timeouts to pinning and model serving endpoints in eu-west-1.

ben (infra): Confirming increased 5xx from infra health checks, spike started ~11:12 UTC. Most errors are client timeouts to endpoints that normally route via eu-west-1 -> provider edge.

carla (sre): Any DNS changes? Some customers show NXDOMAIN for certain subdomains for a minute earlier. Could be incidental or cache churn.

maria (net-oncall): No config changes from our side. I see routes for impacted prefixes flapping with AS_PATH showing AS64521 then disappearing. Looks like an upstream transit instability.

kevin (ndr): Traceroutes show packet loss after provider PoP in FRA, then timeout. TTLs drop at provider AS. Also seeing RPKI not applicable here.

peers-provider-support-bot: Automated alert from provider: "Investigating transit fabric in FRA region - intermittent control-plane instability. Working with backbone ops." Case #PR-8921.

josh (oncall): Quick mitigation options: 1) Prepends to prefer secondary transit (AS64530) for affected prefixes 2) Temporarily divert traffic via our secondary POPs in eu-central-1 3) Ask provider to dampen flaps / blackhole if it's a route leak. Thoughts?

maria (net-oncall): Initiating option 1 and 2 in parallel. Adding 3 if we get confirmation of leak. Applying AS_PATH prepend to affected fronting prefixes now. I'll post command.

maria (net-oncall): ```
# bgp: prepend 3 to main-transit
set policy-options policy-statement PREPEND-TO-64530 term 10 then as-path-prepend "64521 64521 64521"
apply-policy PREPEND-TO-64530 to neighbors 198.51.100.2
```

ben (infra): Increasing origin DNS TTLs to 60s for critical endpoints to help clients failover quicker. Also enabling passive failover to eu-central-1 pool in load balancer for new connections.

carla (sre): I'll rotate canaries to eu-central-1 and monitor error budget. Adding a regression alert if 5xx > 3% for 10m.

maria (net-oncall): Provider responded: they see control-plane flaps on a subset of backbone routers; they are rolling an OS-level fix. ETA unknown. They requested we try traffic steering.

kevin (ndr): After prepends, BGP tables now prefer AS64530 for ~85% of test prefixes. Latency looks slightly higher but stable. Packet loss dropped to ~2% on test paths.

josh (oncall): Good. Can we confirm customer-facing impact improved? Carla?

carla (sre): Post-mitigation metrics: 5xx across affected services down from 6.8% to 1.1% in the last 8m. Some residual errors for long-lived connections that didn't reconnect.

maria (net-oncall): I'll keep prepends in place and set community to no-export on flows that must not leave our secondary transit. Also asked provider to escalate with backbone team.

peers-provider-support-bot: Provider update: rolling fix completed on 2 routers; continuing validation. Observed drop in control-plane flaps. Monitoring for 30m.

ben (infra): Sending out a brief note to customers in impacted orgs with summary + workaround (we recommend reconnecting clients and increasing retry backoff for 5 minutes).

carla (sre): Starting a quick postmortem draft. Root cause likely provider BGP control-plane instability; our mitigation was traffic steering + DNS TTL/ALB failover.

maria (net-oncall): Handoff in 30m to @josh (oncall) for overnight watch. I'll leave prepends for now and will remove once provider confirms full stability.

josh (oncall): Taking handoff. Can you post the exact prefixes and commands you applied? Also please add the provider case link.

maria (net-oncall): Prefixes: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 192.0.2.0/24. Applied prepend policy and LB pool shift. Provider case: https://provider.status/cases/PR-8921

carla (sre): Noted. I'm tagging this incident SEV2 and adding follow-up items: - add automated transit failover playbook - improve canary cross-region coverage - add BGP community-based early detection.

maria (net-oncall): :thumbsup: final note: we should consider a scheduled test of secondary transit and make prepends part of runbook so oncall can trigger faster next time. Leaving handoff message here and marking open until provider confirms no further flaps.

josh (oncall): I acknowledge handoff. Monitoring dashboards + will escalate if flaps recur. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
